label: rem:qns-shell-tail-collapse-interpretation
title: Scope and measured support for the $q$-shell tail collapse
html:
In the physical layer of def:qns-unit-layers the hypotheses of prop:qns-shell-tail-collapse are \varepsilon-free: the viscosity satisfies \nu_{\mathrm{phys}} \geq 1/4 for 1 < q \leq 2, and the active block's physical wavenumbers k_{\mathrm{phys}} = q^n - 1 stay bounded on the substrate window. The proposition therefore delivers a tail bound whose constants survive the classical limit q \to 1^{+}.

Numerical evolution of the DN q-shell system supports each hypothesis along actual trajectories. The dissipation-scale crossing exists at every tested \varepsilon, sits below the Kolmogorov estimate 2^{3/4}\varepsilon^{1/4} in physical wavenumber, and moves toward the infrared as \varepsilon \to 0 (qns-dissipation-scale-probe.witness.json). The per-rung equilibrium ratio stays below 1 on every excited rung — for nearest-neighbour transfer (maximum 0.90), second-neighbour transfer at equal strength (qns-nonlocal-transfer-probe.witness.json), all-pairs geometric coupling at decay \lambda = 0.9 (qns-allpairs-transfer-probe.witness.json), and the modulus dynamics of the complex Sabra system (qns-phase-decorrelation-probe.witness.json). Replacing the Sabra phases by decorrelated ones lowers every tail supremum by factors of 4 to 90 (qns-phase-scramble-probe.witness.json), so the coherent evolution bounded by the proposition is the extremal case within this model class.

The statements are internal to the discrete shell hierarchy of a quantum observable universe. Spatial advection — the transport of structures through physical space by large scales — lies outside every shell model, real or complex, and marks the boundary of what this proposition constrains.
